cells.tense: You are reading the pattern beneath the surface, and this reading is landing well today.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Out of all the open possibilities here, single out what you actually want most. Name it to yourself, just to yourself, and take one step toward it today.
cells.core:
You can see how things work underneath what they look like. Not theory — you read a situation and the mechanism comes up clear, and because it does you can drop the literal details that bog other people down. Nothing in this area has been chosen yet, which is exactly why it's alive. The reading is real, and it frees you as much as it frees anyone you turn it on.

The field here is wide open, and reading it well will get too comfortable if you won't commit it to anything. So commit. Choose the light to steer by — the pull you actually want to follow — and turn toward it. Not the smartest choice, not the most defensible one. The one you would miss most if it never happened, named plainly to yourself, walked toward once today.

cells.tense: You will have mapped every version of what could happen before any of it has actually arrived.
cells.act: give the mess a shape it can be carried in
cells.ask: Open a note and write the three things you're actually worried about right now. Not the analysis, just the three. When you catch the loop running again, add to the list instead of chasing it.
cells.core:
You read patterns at a pitch the moment doesn't call for. Something small happens and the machinery underneath it arrives fully diagrammed, plus three versions of where it's going, plus the version after those. None of it is paranoia exactly — the reading is real, it's just running years past the actual scene. You're braced against a future you've already written in detail and can't write at all.

Here is the way back. That reading needs somewhere to sit so it stops generating scenarios without end. Give the concern one proper shape and give it a home — a short written list, three items, no commentary. Then when the loop starts again you can add to the list instead of riding it. The diagram stays useful on a page. It stops being the master of the room.

cells.tense: You stay at the flat surface of things, and you have stayed there a while now.
cells.act: join the practice the others keep
cells.ask: Find someone whose way of reading things you respect, and ask how they see a situation you're working with. Not for an answer — for how they look at it. Then let it land.
cells.core:
You keep the surface and call it sensible. Ask about the deeper thing and you get the literal version — the facts, the details, the plain account, nothing about what's underneath. Not because you can't read it; the flat version is what's available right now. A lot goes unnamed in how you read your own life, and that sits in the way of the part of you that used to see straight through.

Don't try to fix this with more depth. Go sideways. Find someone whose way of reading a situation is alive and ask them to walk with you through something — not for an answer, just their way of looking, in their voice. Sit with how another person does it. Pattern-reading comes back through contact, not through force. Let their version land without correcting it.

cells.tense: You are working from a pattern that is steering you, and you haven't yet told yourself you're in it.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: Next time someone close is carrying something heavy, sit with them ten minutes without diagnosing it, fixing it, or naming the shape of it. Stay alongside them. Then leave with your own read intact.
cells.core:
There's a pattern in how you move through close relationships. It's quietly steering you — the thing you do when someone gets close, the way you brace, the way you sort people into who gets the real version and who gets the polished one — and you haven't quite said to yourself that it's there. Your reading is sharp. It just hasn't been turned on this yet. So the pattern runs, does its work, and you call the result personality.

The way back goes through one person, in person, without the diagnosis. Sit with someone you trust while they're carrying something hard. Don't name what's underneath it, don't fix it, don't tell them what you see unless they ask. Just be alongside them and let what they're feeling reach you, and stay your own shape while it does. Read the pattern from inside the moment, not above it.

attempts.check: Seat and status are all the record supports; the temptation is to say what the person is like or why they got here, which it doesn't. A reader could fairly object that they do have depth in this part of life and I've drawn the flat face of it — the cells must let them say no and keep the ask. The ask survives being wrong because it's a small act that teaches something either way; the sentence that serves me is anything that sounds like 'you're someone who sees what others miss.'
